Work **in pairs**. You need a **free AI chat assistant** in your browser — any
one you like. Nothing to install in R beyond what you already have.

All three rounds work on **one chart**:

> **In 2007, how much does life expectancy vary within each continent — and
> which country has the lowest life expectancy in each?**

Two rules for today:

- **Write down your minutes** in each round, in the log table at the end. How
  long it took is part of the result.
- Every chunk may fail — that is fine (`error: true` above keeps the document
  rendering). Note *what* failed.

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

gdp_data <- read.csv("data/gdplifexp2007.csv")   # the data from session 8
```

```{r}
#| label: look-at-data
str(gdp_data)
```

# Round 2 · Two routes (15 min)

Choose one route and start the clock.

```text

Chart:   x = ____ , y = ____
         geom(s): ____          (which geom shows variation within a group?)

         Do not write a title, a subtitle or any numbers. I will.
```

```{r}
#| label: route-p

# paste the AI's code here

```

## Route T: the chart template

Start from the **chart template** below. It already has the right chart type
for our question — a box plot per continent with every country on top and one
country labelled — but it shows **GDP per capita** and labels the **richest**
country. Change it yourself until it answers our question. The lines you need
to change are marked `# <- CHANGE`. The same code is in `chart_template.R`
in this project; keep that file for later charts.

You may ask the AI **small** questions only — one function, one argument —
such as *"what does expansion() do in ggplot2?"*. Do not paste the task.

```{r}
#| label: route-t

base_size <- 14   # font size of the whole chart: larger for slides
edge_space <- expansion(mult = 0.1)  # 10% extra room at both ends of the
                                     # x-axis, so that no label is cut off


# 1. The number for the title -- computed, never typed ----------------------

spread <- gdp_data |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(ratio = max(gdpPercap) / min(gdpPercap))      # <- CHANGE

asia_ratio <- spread$ratio[spread$continent == "Asia"]    # <- CHANGE


# 2. The countries that get a label: one per continent ----------------------

label_data <- gdp_data |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  slice_max(gdpPercap, n = 1)    # <- CHANGE: slice_max() = highest,
                                 #    slice_min() = lowest


# 3. The chart ---------------------------------------------------------------

my_chart <- ggplot(
  data = gdp_data,
  # the variable on x, the groups on y: long group names stay readable
  mapping = aes(x = gdpPercap, y = continent)              # <- CHANGE
) +
  # the box: median, middle half of the countries, and the range.
  # outlier.shape = NA hides the box's own outlier dots, because the
  # points below show every country anyway
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6, colour = "grey50") +
  # every country as one point; alpha = 0.4 makes them see-through, so
  # where many countries overlap, the colour gets darker
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 2.5, colour = "#00395B") +
  # the labelled countries again, on top and in red ...
  geom_point(data = label_data, size = 3, colour = "#E65032") +
  # ... and their names, placed just above each box
  geom_text(
    data = label_data, mapping = aes(label = country),
    nudge_y = 0.4, size = base_size / 3.5, colour = "#E65032") +

  # x-axis: keep ONE of the two lines, put a # in front of the other.
  # log axis: for skewed variables such as income or population
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1), expand = edge_space) +
  # linear axis: for most other variables, e.g. life expectancy
  # scale_x_continuous(expand = edge_space) +

  labs(
    # the title states the finding, with the number computed above
    title = paste0("In Asia, the richest country is ", round(asia_ratio),
                   " times as rich as the poorest"),      # <- CHANGE
    subtitle = "GDP per capita, 142 countries, 2007",     # <- CHANGE
    x = "GDP per capita (log scale)",                     # <- CHANGE: with unit
    y = NULL,                       # the continent names speak for themselves
    caption = "Data: Gapminder."    # always name the source
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
  theme(
    plot.title            = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title.position   = "plot",     # title flush with the left edge
    plot.caption          = element_text(colour = "grey45", hjust = 1),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    panel.grid.minor      = element_blank(),  # fewer lines, less clutter
    legend.position       = "top",      # if you add a legend: on top, left
    legend.justification  = "left"
  )

my_chart
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hints for route T — open only if you are stuck
1. Replace `gdpPercap` by `lifeExp` everywhere it is marked `# <- CHANGE`.
2. Life expectancy is not skewed like income: put a `#` in front of the
   `scale_x_log10()` line and remove the `#` in front of
   `scale_x_continuous()`.
3. Our question asks for the **lowest** country: `slice_min()` instead of
   `slice_max()`.
4. A ratio of life expectancies makes little sense. Compute the
   **difference** instead: `max(lifeExp) - min(lifeExp)`, and rewrite the
   title around it.
5. Update the subtitle and the x-axis label — with the unit.
:::

the chart code does.

# If you finish early ⭐

a) **Ask twice.** Send your route P prompt again, in a new chat. Same code?
   Same chart?

b) **The other route.** Do the route your pair did not do. Which was faster?

c) **The average.** Ask your assistant for *"the average life expectancy per
   continent"*. Does it weight countries by population? Should it? (Think of
   China and India.)

d) **Make it a snippet.** Save the chart template as an RStudio snippet
   (*Tools → Edit Code Snippets*, see the appendix of the slides) and insert
   it with its name and <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd>.

e) **Explain it back.** Ask the assistant to explain one line of your final
   code that you did not fully understand. Then close the chat and explain the
   line to your partner.
